comments: Toootally did not go to class. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The clause that he kills time is accurately carried into the following unit.
Together with the preceding clause, the English accurately says he passes time until evening.

adjudicated.en: Is Senpai still around, I wonder?
comments: Not a bad question considering she sometimes jump. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His wondering whether his senior is still present is functionally preserved under the translation's retained-address convention.

adjudicated.jp: 記憶とともに、温度もゆるくなったようだ。
adjudicated.en: The temperature seems to have become more lenient together with the recollections.
comments: He's totally starting to forget whether Misato was up there. That's the result of those flashbacks he possibly had off-screen. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The temperature or heat seems to have eased along with the memories. Calling temperature 'lenient' is a lexical calque, while 'together with the recollections' fails to express the parallel softening naturally.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The heat seemed to have softened along with the memories.'

highlights.text: more lenient together with the recollections

adjudicated.jp: 屋上から見渡せた藍色の帳は、すでに緋色に染め直されている。
adjudicated.en: The curtain of indigo blue I could see on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back into a brilliant scarlet.
comments: Supposing it's 6PM. This should be 2AM. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The indigo curtain visible from the rooftop has already been redyed scarlet. The English changes the rooftop into the object looked over, uses the calque 'passing my sight,' and makes the curtain intransitively dye itself.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The indigo curtain I had seen from the rooftop was already dyed scarlet.'

highlights.text: on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back

adjudicated.jp: 吹きつけていた突風もない。
adjudicated.en: The squall that was blowing against is gone.
comments: See CCA0006. Since the wind = the pretense, and Misato is asleep, ergo SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The gusts that had been blasting across the rooftop are gone. 'Blowing against' requires an object, leaving the English clause grammatically incomplete.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The gusts that had been buffeting the rooftop were gone too.'

adjudicated.jp: 去勢された猫のようにおとなしい、黄昏の頃。
adjudicated.en: The time of twilight is as docile as an emasculated cat.
comments: Taichi, well emasculated from soon after birth, yet struggling with a monster that repeatedly takes the form of his dick, and who can't stand the blood that is evening to the point of hallucinating that the twilasdiujdveSYMBOLISM!!1! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The simile specifies a castrated cat. 'Emasculated' is normally applied figuratively to people or institutions and sounds like an accidental thesaurus substitution rather than the blunt animal image.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Twilight was as docile as a neutered cat.'

adjudicated.assessment: The statement that no one is there is exact.

adjudicated.en: I search for signs of Misato-senpai.
adjudicated.assessment: Searching for signs of her presence is a defensible contextual rendering of looking for her figure.
The brief sound of recognition is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: アンテナが佇むのその隣で。
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment locates her beside the standing antenna. 'Neighboring' makes the subject itself adjacent as a participial action, and 'stillstanding' is not a standard compound in this use.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Beside the standing antenna,'

adjudicated.assessment: Within present-tense discovery, he says 'There she is.' The past-tense English turns the immediate recognition into retrospective narration.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There she is.'

adjudicated.assessment: The compact observation that she is sleeping is preserved as a fragment.
The silent line is exact. Its canonical occurrence is topology-resolved between the immediately preceding and following bound records in the same source file.
The source describes light, regular sleeping breaths. 'A light sleeper's breathing' instead characterizes the person as easily awakened, while the postposed 'regular' leaves the phrase malformed.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Light, regular sleeping breaths.'

adjudicated.jp: 雑音に過ぎないそれは、不思議な音楽性を伴って思考を弛緩させる。
adjudicated.en: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax.
comments: See CCA0006. This is far closer to pretty than to purple, but it's still fairly overwrought. And what he's about to do isn't changing. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Though merely noise, the breathing has a mysterious musicality that relaxes his thoughts. The English is syntactically incoherent, recasts 'no more than noise' as failure to transcend a specific noise, and never establishes the causal relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Though it was only noise, its strange musicality relaxed my thoughts.'

highlights.text: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax

adjudicated.jp: 吸って、吐いて、吸って、吐いて。
adjudicated.en: Inhale, then exhale, then inhale, then exhale.
adjudicated.assessment: The rhythmic inhalation and exhalation sequence is exact.
The gentle, harmless breath is accurately rendered.

adjudicated.jp: 飾り気のない、彼女の自然体の姿。
adjudicated.en: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned.
adjudicated.assessment: The source presents her unadorned, natural self. The English's noun stack is ungrammatical, and 'natural in posture' narrows 自然体 into physical posture rather than unselfconscious being.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her natural, unadorned self.'

highlights.text: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned

adjudicated.assessment: The absence of falsehood is accurately carried into the following fragment.
The paired fragment says there is no stain or impurity either. 'Filth neither' is not grammatical English and is harsher and more concrete than the abstract moral image.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'nor any stain.'

adjudicated.jp: 眠りのときは、誰もが無垢な時代に戻る。
adjudicated.en: All return to a time of purity when they sleep.
comments: chidlren go 2 heaven -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The idea that sleep returns everyone to an earlier state of innocence or purity is preserved.
The source is the adverbial fragment 'still' or 'without moving.' The English adds the act of staring and uses the markedly unnatural adverb 'motionlessly.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Motionless.' or, if the carried context requires it, 'I stared without moving.'

adjudicated.jp: 奪われた視線を、世界を包む薄暮の鮮やかさでさえ取り戻せない。
adjudicated.en: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back by the mere vividness of the dusk that clads the world.
adjudicated.assessment: His gaze has been captured, and even the vivid twilight enveloping the world cannot win it back. The apparent typo 'said' removes the gaze entirely, 'forcibly stolen' overstates 奪われた, and the passive construction obscures what cannot reclaim it.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Even the vivid twilight enveloping the world could not reclaim my captured gaze.'

highlights.text: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back

adjudicated.assessment: The duration fragment is accurately carried into the following sentence.
He watches his senior for a long time; the action is exact under the retained-address convention.
The paired envy and longing or admiration are preserved.
The silent line is exact. Its canonical occurrence is topology-resolved between the immediately preceding and following bound records in the same source file.

adjudicated.jp: どれくらい、そうしていたのか。
adjudicated.en: For how long did I stay like that?
comments: Loss of time perception. Still. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His wondering how long he remained like that is naturally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: すこやかな寝息はおさまり、まぶたが震えた。
adjudicated.en: A more vigorous breath the conclusion, her eyelids quivered,
adjudicated.assessment: Her peaceful sleeping breaths subside and her eyelids tremble. The English fragment is syntactically incoherent, turns healthy or sound breathing into 'more vigorous' breathing, and does not state that it stops.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her peaceful breathing subsided, and her eyelids trembled.'

highlights.text: A more vigorous breath the conclusion

adjudicated.jp: 長い睫毛が小刻みに痙攣する。
adjudicated.en: her long eyelashes tremble in a quivering motion,
adjudicated.assessment: Her long eyelashes twitch in tiny movements. 'Tremble in a quivering motion' is tautological and replaces the sharper involuntary twitch with a redundant phrase.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'her long eyelashes twitching rapidly,'

adjudicated.en: and the eyes opened, a sliver.
adjudicated.assessment: Her eyes opening only a sliver is accurately conveyed in compressed prose.

comments: Sooo very off tone. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His renewed admiration for his senior is functionally conveyed, with slightly heightened enthusiasm.
The drowsy, confused vocalization is functionally represented.

adjudicated.jp: 言語感覚が鈍った先輩は、童女の如くあどけない声を立てた。
adjudicated.en: Her linguistic senses blunted, Senpai had a cherubic voice like a little girl's.
comments: Matt 18:3. She can return to a child, ergo she can be forgiven. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her language faculties being dulled by sleep and her innocent, childlike voice are both substantially preserved.

comments: /sarc -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The polite morning greeting is naturally rendered.
The hesitant name and retained suffix are exact under the translation's address convention.
He corrects her with 'It's Peke.' The subject-complement inversion is not motivated by the source and gives him an affected, non-native syntax.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It's Peke.'

adjudicated.assessment: She sleepily repeats the exclusive nickname with its retained suffix.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩専用のニックネームを、彼女が復唱する。
adjudicated.en: Senpai repeats that nickname that is for her exclusive use.
comments: Going with this: it'll be even more obvious, later, when Miki starts calling her "Mimi-senpai" as well, as she's not supposed to. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narration accurately identifies the nickname as reserved for her use and says that she repeats it.
Her drowsy protest is 'Mm, no...' or 'I don't like that...' The bare adjective 'not nice' is childlike in a different way and does not form a natural response to the situation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use '...Mm, no...'

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Seeing my sleeping face, not nice..."
comments: Childish -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She objects to his having seen her sleeping face. The fragment makes her own act of seeing the grammatical subject and again substitutes the malformed 'not nice' for her embarrassed refusal.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You saw me sleeping... no...'

highlights.text: Seeing my sleeping face, not nice

adjudicated.jp: 二の腕でいちどきに双眸を覆い、かすかに身もだえる。
adjudicated.en: She writhes slightly, both arms covering the both of her eyes.
comments: Back to purple: zero need whatsoever to use that OMFG HARD KANJI's for "pair of eyes" here. Or pretty much ever. I'd translate it to "binocular", but I have standards dammit. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She covers both eyes at once with one upper arm and writhes faintly. The English changes that singular upper arm into both arms, repeats 'both' ungrammatically, and obscures the specific pose.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She covered both eyes with one upper arm and squirmed faintly.'

highlights.text: both arms covering the both of her eyes

adjudicated.jp: 無防備な自分の姿は、誰だって隠したい。
adjudicated.en: Anyone would want to conceal their most defenseless of appearances.
adjudicated.assessment: Anyone would want to hide their unguarded self. The superlative-plus-of construction is ungrammatical and turns a general state of vulnerability into an oddly ranked appearance.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Anyone would want to hide such an unguarded side of themselves.'

adjudicated.jp: 隠したいということは、普段の自分に嘘があるということで。
adjudicated.en: But the concealment itself means that there are lies in one's normal self.
adjudicated.assessment: The inference that wanting concealment implies falsehood in one's ordinary self is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.en: Is it then the same for Senpai?
adjudicated.assessment: His question whether the same applies to her is exact under the retained-address convention.
He cuts off and discards the cold line of thought; the metaphor is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: やがて先輩は身を起こす。
adjudicated.en: Before long, Senpai raises herself up.
adjudicated.assessment: Her sitting or raising herself up after a moment is accurately conveyed.

comments: Not wholly awake. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The question is accurate, but the detached apostrophe before 've' is not a valid contraction and visibly corrupts the line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'How long have you been there?'

comments: Immediate lie... or is it? See CCX0001: hours aren't seconds for him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He answers 'Just now.' The plural noun phrase is incomplete English and suggests an unspecified number of moments rather than immediate arrival.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Just now.'

adjudicated.assessment: Her doubtful hum is functionally represented.
The suspicious gaze is accurately rendered.

comments: As above, it may be. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His insistence that he is telling the truth is accurate, though formal.

adjudicated.jp: 両手をあげて、降参してみる。
adjudicated.en: I raise both hands and attempt surrender.
comments: See CCA0006, which is why he did the same there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He raises both hands in a show of surrender. 'Attempt surrender' is missing the infinitive marker or nominal preposition and sounds like a failed tactical action rather than a gesture.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I raised both hands in surrender.'

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩に嘘なんてつきませんよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I would never lie to you, Senpai!"
comments: Well, deceptions aren't lies, are there. After all, there's no lie about the end of mankind if Taichi is convinced that's true. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His assurance that he would never lie to her is naturally conveyed under the retained-address convention.
The silent line is exact. Its canonical occurrence is topology-resolved between the immediately preceding and following bound records in the same source file.

adjudicated.jp: 「でも、日中は寝こけないようにしないと危ないですよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day!"
comments: Misato's sleep patterns are also broken. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He warns that it is dangerous to let herself fall asleep during the day. The nested negative 'not to ensure you do not' makes the condition difficult to parse and reverses its force on a first reading.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'But you shouldn't fall asleep during the day. It's dangerous.'

highlights.text: it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day

adjudicated.jp: 「脱水症状や日射病になったら危険ですもん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Dehydrating or catching sunstroke will put you in serious danger."
comments: Forget no doctors, since Gunjou doesn't care (under the guise of freedom), nobody'll be there to help her and she'll probably die. To nobody caring. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The danger of dehydration or sunstroke is accurately conveyed, despite a slightly awkward gerund.
Her sleepy agreement is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.en: She kills a yawn in her teeth.
comments: Just look at that sentence! Unnecessarily using kanji that require furries for something as simple as a 'yawn', and an apparently simple sentence ("stifling e.g. a yawn") that also means "to bite do death", as well as containing the kanji for 'kill' fairly literally. Ugly in surface, evocative underneath: Touko is known to kill stuff in her mouth, for starters, as well as subject to dehydration (and starvation). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The idiom means that she stifles or suppresses a yawn. The English renders both halves literally and adds 'in her teeth,' producing an image and construction that do not exist in idiomatic English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She stifled a yawn.'

highlights.text: kills a yawn in her teeth

adjudicated.assessment: Her glasses having slipped down or out of place is accurately conveyed.

comments: Everybody dazzled from the big words above, or are you not missing this? See CCA0009B. Fixed existence... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His hand reaches out before he can help himself. 'My hand stretched' describes the hand lengthening or extending itself and omits the directional particle needed for the involuntary gesture.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'My hand reached out before I knew it.'

adjudicated.assessment: Her quiet surprise is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 眼鏡を両手で挟み、顔を寄せて、そっと元に戻す。
adjudicated.en: With both hands I seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face.
comments: No choice, but he knows his limits. "Return to origin", see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He cups the glasses with both hands, leans his face closer, and gently puts them back in place. 'Seize' makes the touch forceful, 'return them to normal' mistakes position for condition, and 'close to the face' relocates rather than describes his approach.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I took her glasses between both hands, leaned close, and gently set them back in place.'

highlights.text: seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face

adjudicated.assessment: He says that this restores her usual appearance. The English is a malformed fragment that lacks the idiomatic demonstrative or copula needed to complete the thought.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There. Now you're the Senpai I know.'

comments: Because she knows he wanted to go for her boobs... or does she? And did he? More below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her embarrassed complaint means roughly 'Honestly, that was risky.' The English supplies two unsupported intensifiers but no natural clause, making her reaction sound like a label rather than speech.
adjudicated.remedy: Use '...Honestly. That was dangerous.'

adjudicated.jp: 「ぺけくんのそういうところ、危険です」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "That part of you is dangerous, Peke-kun."
adjudicated.assessment: She accurately identifies that side of him as dangerous, retaining the private form of address.

adjudicated.jp: 少し怒っている気がする。
adjudicated.en: It feels like she's a little angry.
adjudicated.assessment: His impression that she seems a little angry is exact.
His two-part demand to know what she means and why is preserved.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Do look at a mirror and think about this."
comments: Despite the thing about the boobs, she might just not like people sneaking up to others, seeing CCA0006, CCD1001, and parts of Youko. Of course she does it herself, that's how she knows his smile is fake, see CCE0001. Sentence should refer to 長生きしたい人は鏡を見なさい, those who want a long life should look in a mirror.

The sentence, silly Misato, means external looks are a reflection of one's internal health, not simply to reflect on one's actions, so she screwed this up bad. This scene is where cross communication really starts, so pay attention. Come the Kiri route... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She tells him to look in a mirror and think about it. 'Look at a mirror' makes the physical object the target rather than his reflection and weakens the idiomatic rebuke.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Look in a mirror and think about it.'

adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated cry of offended surprise is functionally represented.

adjudicated.jp: うわ、泣きそうなこと言った、この人！
adjudicated.en: Bwah, this person here's just said something that makes me cry!
adjudicated.assessment: He exclaims that she said something liable to make him cry. The demonstrative-person calque is unnatural, and 'makes me cry' turns the near-tears reaction into a categorical present fact.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Whoa—she said something that could make me cry!'

highlights.text: this person here's just said something that makes me cry

adjudicated.jp: 「俺が不細工ってことですかぁーっ！　うわあああ、気にしてるのにー！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Is it because I am horrendooous! Bwaaaaaah, when I worry so much about thaaat!!!"
comments: The term used is literally "a poor-quality product". Ties well into him being a product of God and all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He wails that he is sensitive about being ugly. 'When I worry' introduces a temporal subordinate clause with no main-clause relation and misses the idiomatic sense of being self-conscious about it.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'And I'm already so self-conscious about it!'

highlights.text: when I worry so much about thaaat

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Eh, that is not what I..."
adjudicated.assessment: Her interrupted denial is naturally preserved.

comments: Oddly he generally uses 母 to refers to his mother, this is probably terminology inconsistency. Mother coming out in times of panic is so literally true. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The melodramatic self-denigration and infantile address are functionally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「あああ、違います、違いますってば、ね？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Ahhh, you are mistaken, I am telling you that you are mistaken, OK?"
comments: See CCZAS, this is very similar to her panicking as Taichi goes to "kill" her. Parallel Miki: this is the entirety of his psychotic attacks, and the rest are just him rationalizing them as far worse. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her increasingly emphatic reassurance that he is mistaken is preserved, though verbose.
The deliberately childish complaint that his mother gave birth to him ugly is preserved.
The adaptation naturally conveys her syllable-by-syllable insistence that he listen.

adjudicated.jp: 「いいんです、どーせブッサーなんです。大自然の一部なんです。キモダンなんです」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It is fine, I am revolting anyway. It is just part of the natural order. I am nothing but a gross creep."
comments: "Bussah" http://www28.atwiki.jp/minaqua/pages/2636.html More of a direct interest that odd thing about his ugliness being "part of the natural order": see CCC4025, consistent with Miki talking about "a Taichi of this world", consistent with the idea that his hideousness - whether murderous impulses or something less - are something that comes from this world, not higher sources. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The escalating comic self-insults are functionally represented, though the coined-word texture is necessarily reduced.

adjudicated.jp: 「いえ、そんなことは……確かに最初に会ったときはおどろかされましたけど」

His reply isn't given, however, so maybe he turned her down really nastily. Or perhaps it's just to further the idea that Misato has serious problems expressing herself in a way that's not self-damaging, certainly a callback to the concept of Incommunicability, as mentioned by Thomas Aquinas it is a possible part of--- uhm, that joke about Italian cinema in the '60s and '70s I had here fell off the back and got run over. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her denial followed by the damaging concession about their first meeting is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぎゅわーーーーーーーーーーーーーっ！？」

adjudicated.jp: 「わっ、ぺけくんがおかしな具合に！」

comments: Sorta-softwareish. He did just crash. -GHS

adjudicated.jp: 「我ガ名ハクリエイター、人類ノ支配存在デアル！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE THE BEING THAT DOMINATES MANKIND!"
comments: The stupid old ROM wouldn't really accept Western characters unless I hacked the graphics drawing program and had it insert the text manually, which isn't not very elegant due to double-byte characters in the original Japanese (technical hacking stuff, don't mind it), so it read like all centered and with lots of spaces and stuff, but then my editor (which is inexplicably a sock puppet) begged me to use the bootleg that runs on Scramble hardware (MAME joke) so that mere caps are sufficient. Stupid tween who's never been in an arcade in the 80s grumble grumble gitoffmahlawn a fie on both his house and the basement he lives in grumble. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-archaic declaration is singular: 'My name is Creator; I am the being who rules humanity.' The English is ungrammatical and changes both singular first-person claims into plural ones.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a deliberately archaic but grammatical singular declaration.

highlights.text: WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE

adjudicated.jp: 「わ、わ、ぺけくんが二十年前のゲームのボスみたいな陳腐な創造主に！？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Wah, wah, Peke-kun has become an hackneyed Creator of All Life like some boss from a 20-year old videogame?!"
comments: Beware, he lives! Well, the reference is too vague, I only suspect Sinistar because of tone. Also "I hunger!" works with Taichi the Devourer of All Things (in his mind). The rest is religious, but I don't see how anyone could be stumped by a guy who was likely retrained via videogames and spouts sub-Nietzscheian nonsense at the drop of a hat thinking he's a hackneyed videogame God from the '80s after being struck in a very delicate spot. I mean, DUH. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She calls him a hackneyed creator like a boss from a game twenty years ago. The English uses the wrong article and adds the unsupported scope 'of All Life.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a hackneyed creator' without the added domain.

highlights.text: an hackneyed Creator of All Life

adjudicated.jp: 「ナニユエ我ニ逆ラウノカ。我ノ支配ノナカニイレバ、永遠ノ平和ヲ手ニ入レルコトガデキヨウ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "FOR WHAT PURPOSE DO YOU OPPOSE US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL IS TO OBTAIN PEACE ETERNAL."
comments: See CCC3013 as well: the final boss of Phantasy Star II fits. Perhaps a conflation of Sinistar and PS2, actually, it would fit very well with Taichi's memory. This question is Jesus in a nutshell. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker asks why she opposes him and promises that entering his rule would let her obtain eternal peace. The English again changes singular 'me/my' to plural 'us/our' and turns the conditional promise into an abstract equation.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the singular ruler and the conditional relation.

highlights.text: US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL
